newsitem.title: UK: London gold touch firmer after Buba, PGMs soar.
newsitem.headline: London gold touch firmer after Buba, PGMs soar.

text.p: Gold prices ambled gently higher on Thursday as the platinum group metals (PGMs) continued the climb which attained fresh high ground on Wednesday.

Dealers said the rift between the Bundesbank and German government on revaluing gold reserves was potentially bullish for bullion but the sheer lack of platinum and palladium availability was the dominating factor in the precious metals sector.
Gold was fixed at $345.70 per ounce up from $342.80 on Wednesday's afternoon fix and against a close of $344.80/$345.30.
Late on Wednesday the Bundesbank rejected Bonn's plans to revalue its assets, including gold, as the government attempted to cut deficits to within European Monetary Union (EMU) criteria.
"There has been no real impact from the Bundesbank (on gold) but it is potentially bullish. We could end up with EMU itself shot down before it evens starts," one dealer said.
He added that more significantly for the market the spat in Germany probably made it less likely that other European central banks would sell gold in the short term.
However market attention was riveted on platinum and palladium which had a turbulent time on Wednesday with spot prices rocking through ranges of around $20.
Jitters were not calmed by the ending of an unofficial strike by some workers at the Rustenburg mine in South Africa with little loss of production.
Platinum fixed at its highest level since February 21 1996 at $417.50 up from $399.50 on Wednesday and palladium was fixed at $196.50, its highest fix since fixings began in 1989.
It was last around that level in October 1980 when the month's average palladium price was $201.00, according to U.S. Bureau of Mines statistics.
Lack of metal was the dominant factor, dealers said.
"There is so much tightness in the spot market," one dealer said adding that dealers were charging 33 percent to lend platinum for a month and palladium was commanding 45-50 percent.
"The (buy-sell) spreads are so wide this market could do anything, and with such a large backwardation it could turn just like that and it will be horrendous," a dealer said.
Russia the largest exporter of palladium and second largest supplier of platinum has not shipped metal all year due to administration problems.
Silver was virtually untouched by moves elsewhere and was quoted two cents firmer at $4.73/$4.75.
